newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa a shade lower, digests recent gains.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa a shade lower, digests recent gains.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures were a touch lower by midsession on Wednesday on light profit-taking amid perceptions that the recent steep run-up could have been a bit overdone.
"This morning's performance is a bit disappointing to the bulls who are expecting the market to jump higher," said one trader.
There was also a growing feeling that the New York market could face a downward correction following the current rally which had pushed prices to nine-year highs.
Benchmark September was four stg down at 1,142 stg a tonne after a high of 1,150. The contract hit a one-year high of 1,162 on Tuesday.
December was also four stg lower at 1,143 and total turnover was 3,079 lots.
While the overall technical outlook remains buoyant, traders said the market was not backed by solid fundamentals.
"Fundamentally, it is trading on a flimsy foundation," said one.
The dry spell expected later this year following the El Nino weather may affect the crop in the longer term but in the immediate term, West Africa is receiving above average rainfall.
"This is why people call it a silly season...this is the time prices go up," the trader said.
